source_title: Former teacher Tayla Lee Brailey jailed for sex acts with students
source_excerpt:
Tayla Lee Brailey pleaded guilty to having sex with two students under her care and exchanging child abuse material. ( Facebook )
A woman who taught at a Sydney high school has been given a 15-month prison sentence for sexual offences involving two male students.
Tayla Lee Brailey appeared in Parramatta District Court today after pleading guilty to four charges relating to sex acts committed against two teenage students in 2024, including using a carriage service to transmit and access child abuse material.
Judge Elizabeth Ryan said the manner in which Brailey had broken the trust between teacher and student warranted a custodial sentence.
"Offences like this cause immense harm to the trust that must exist between families and the education system," Judge Ryan said.
"For these reasons … no penalty other than imprisonment is appropriate."
Tayla Lee Brailey was first charged by police at a high school in Sydney in August 2024. ( Facebook )
Brailey was first arrested by detectives at a Sydney school in August 2024, when she was charged with offences relating to sexual touching and sexual intercourse with a person under special care.
After being released on bail, she was arrested again less than two weeks later and charged with multiple sex offences relating to a second teenage student.
The court heard Brailey had initiated contact with one teenager.
Tayla Lee Brailey was sentenced by Judge Elizabeth Ryan at Parramatta District Court. ( ABC News: Abubakr Sajid )
Reading a victim impact statement prepared by one of the teenagers, the judge said the offending had a deep impact on the students.
"He wrote that he has been feeling ashamed and had to leave high school before he finished year 12, because of the shame he felt," the judge said.
"He had suffered lack of sleep and flashbacks … he said none of his friends at high school speaks to him anymore.
The judge also acknowledged letters submitted by members of Brailey's family, which said the 32-year-old's crimes had cost her a husband, her job and reputation.
Reading a psychologist's report tendered to the court, the judge said Brailey had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and was likely experiencing a manic episode at the time of the offending.
"In July 2024, Ms Brailey made terrible mistakes," the judge said.
"She used her position as a teacher … to abuse the trust of two young persons."
Brailey will be eligible for parole on April 24, 2027.
The judge ordered that she be placed on the NSW Police child protection register for 15 years.
